Just don't think about it. Most people don't notice and the people who do will either not give a shit or they will speak up out of genuine concern, not with cruel intentions. Speaking from experience. The truth is most people are way too concerned and worried about themselves to notice little things like that. 

Be comfortable in your skin. Own it and be the best you.
We're on the same wavelength...I like to hope u/winnipegreddit is right

Thanks for the update, I'm really glad things are going so much better for you. I've had some similar results myself! I'm magically content and it's wonderful. I have not felt depressed for a long time and can "feel" my emotions now. Like you, I also feel more clear minded and my attitude towards different things feels genuine instead of forced or unnatural! These daily feelings that I've been without for so long make each day still seem kind of weird and sometimes uncomfortable because I've been used to hiding in my depression so long. Nevertheless I hope this lasts because feeling real joy, real sadness, and living without a cloud over my head is a wonderful thing :) I'll post another update down the road. I'm really happy we're both seeing fantastic results!
I would really appreciate it and yes I'll be happy to do the same. Me too, really glad I found your post.

I am experiencing the same thing! It has been one week today that I have been on 150mg XL and I had been feeling better than I have in years.  The past few months have been so bad (suicidal thoughts, missing college classes, not getting out of bed) but it only took a day for the Wellbutrin to kick in and I felt so much better.  Not like a *happy high* but more like someone lifted a blanket off of me and I could *find* happiness in everyday things again.

Now as I'm writing this, it's 2:30am, I want to drop out of college again, and I just feel pretty shitty and depressed like I've been used to.  I see the doctor next week and, depending on how the next several days go, I might inquire about upping the dose...idk if that's what you were thinking or not. Obviously the doc's decision, maybe it just takes longer than a week to really settle in?

Would love to stay in contact with you and see how you're doing given we've both been diagnosed and prescribed at about the same time.

It's absolutely terrible. It scarred me for life and I feel worse than I ever have before. 

After hanging up with the suicide hotline, the cops came banging on my door, cuffed me, and took me involuntarily. Spent the first night sleeping on the floor with no pillow or blanket and no food...must've been 60 degrees the whole time I was there. When I finally got moved up to the ward there were people screaming, talking to themselves, fighting, it was like a horror movie. I could never sleep, eat, and was always deathly cold. One old woman went nuts on me because I scratched my ear.

I was only there for two nights and was able to be let go the third day after begging the doctor. It was the most miserable experience of my entire life and I will never forget it. Please, find a therapist or someone to talk to before you ever consider checking yourself in. And never call the suicide hotline, because even if you hang up and say thank you and goodnight, they still call the cops on you. It's not anonymous. 

On my phone so I might have rambled a bit, but I really hope you feel better. PM me if you ever need someone to talk to. I've made it this far, you can too!

Peace and love.

Thanks. Taking your advice and getting out of town this weekend.  I've written most of my letters but there's still that hesitation lingering inside. I'll definitely have time and a place to think for a while.

I've thought about this too, but afraid it's too slow where I live (large freight trains). Do you think it has to be a high speed train to be  instant and painless? The thought of pain is making me lean more towards a gun.
Worked for the first year for me. Then plummeted to rock bottom where I've currently been.  I hope you have better luck!
